intro: Column missing rates can hide rows where several features disappear together. A joint audit reports both marginal rates and pairwise co-missingness.
task: Report marginal and pairwise missingness to distinguish jointly missing features from disjoint missingness patterns.
requirements: mask is a two-dimensional NumPy boolean array with at least one row and one column. True means missing.
Return dict feature_rates (column means), row_counts (missing count per row as integer array), and co_missing (feature-by-feature matrix of mean pairwise AND).
The diagonal of co_missing equals feature_rates. Pairwise values are joint fractions, not correlations or conditional probabilities.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Convert before multiplying
hints.body: Boolean matrix multiplication does not produce integer co-occurrence counts; cast the mask.

hints.title: Normalize by rows
hints.body: Divide pairwise counts by the total number of observations.

explanation: Marginal missingness rates summarize individual features, while joint rates reveal whether features tend to disappear in the same rows. The diagonal is a useful internal consistency check.
Joint missingness is not evidence of a causal mechanism. This audit provides observable counts that can guide data collection checks and later modeling choices.
